review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the Laplace kernel file's `laplaceTransformENN` API, Mathlib's `mgf_smul_measure`, and the repository uses of `laplaceTransform_apply`, `laplaceTransform_zero`, `laplaceTransform_smul_measure` and `toReal_laplaceTransformENN`. The existing simp set looks coherent: `laplaceTransform_zero`, `laplaceTransform_zero_measure` and `laplaceTransform_dirac` are all oriented toward simpler forms. I found no loop. The deliberate choice not to make `laplaceTransform_apply` simp is documented and reasonable, so I did not flag it. Both findings are modest and rest on reading the sources, not on running Lean. In both cases I am uncertain whether the added simp attribute would help beyond the two or three proofs inside this file.

findings.excerpt: laplaceTransform (c • μ) t = c.toReal * laplaceTransform μ t
findings.problem: This is an unconditional equation with no hypotheses. It rewrites the transform of a scaled measure to the transform of the base measure, which is smaller. It sits beside the simp lemmas `laplaceTransform_zero_measure` and `laplaceTransform_dirac` and is the natural normal-form rule for scalar multiples. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. Mathlib's `mgf_smul_measure` is not simp either, so nothing else covers this case. Both users in the file (lines 573 and 677) need a manual `rw [laplaceTransform_smul_measure, ENNReal.coe_toReal, ...]`, because simp would not normalise `((c : ℝ≥0∞) • μ)`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `laplaceTransform_smul_measure` with `@[simp]`. The `c.toReal` term then normalises through the existing simp lemma `ENNReal.coe_toReal` when `c` is a coercion from `ℝ≥0`. Check that no competing simp lemma fires on `c • μ` inside `laplaceTransform`. In the two `RepresentsLaplace*.smul` proofs, `rw [...]` could then become a `simp`-based step.
findings.benefit: Expressions such as `laplaceTransform (c • μ) t` would reduce automatically to a multiple of the base transform. Proofs about scaled representing measures would no longer need to name the lemma and then `ENNReal.coe_toReal` by hand.

evidence.excerpt: lemma mgf_smul_measure (c : ℝ≥0∞) : mgf X (c • μ) t = c.toReal * mgf X μ t

findings.problem: This is the only bridge from the extended-real `laplaceTransformENN` to the real `laplaceTransform`. It is oriented from the more elaborate form to the base one, and its only side condition is the instance `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, which simp can discharge by instance search. It is not `@[simp]`. The file's own statement `representsLaplace_laplaceTransformENN` has the shape `(laplaceTransformENN μ t.toNNReal).toReal`, which the bridge would reduce, and it is currently handled by hand with `rw [toReal_laplaceTransformENN, Real.coe_toNNReal t ht]`. Similarly, `laplaceTransformENN_eq` rewrites in reverse with `← toReal_laplaceTransformENN`. Both users must invoke the bridge manually.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `toReal_laplaceTransformENN` with `@[simp]`, so that `(laplaceTransformENN μ t).toReal` normalises to `laplaceTransform μ ↑t` under a finite-measure instance. Do not also add a competing lemma that expands `laplaceTransform` to an integral. This keeps `laplaceTransform` as the single real-valued normal form.
findings.benefit: Statements that mix the two transforms (for example the represented-function predicate over `laplaceTransformENN`) would simplify to the real transform automatically. The bridge would no longer need to be cited in each proof.
